title: The Fullness of God and the Myth of Lethe
english: God fills all things, without being limited by anything. For he who is not limited by place will be entirely in every place, according to the hymn of David. If it were said that he is outside of any place, it is necessary that he be limited by that which he is fixed to; therefore, becoming whole in all things, he does not move from one place to another while filling all.
The divine is not subject to description by explicit laws and temporal accounts.

But since they clearly know themselves to have been caught here, moving about, they muddy the water of forgetfulness, which they say causes each to forget the births of their own lives. Since these things are mythical and far from philosophy, no one of sound mind seems to be ignorant. For what do we say, O Pythagoreans and Platonists: did you yourselves drink the water that causes forgetfulness after taking it, or on the contrary do you flee it?
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
